owner_posts.post_text:
Important Update About Our Practice : 

Acumed Veterinary Specialty will now become an exclusive Neurology Practice, the OPD / General Practice will close down soon. 

After 12 years of caring for your companions, we are writing to share that Acumed's OPD / General Practice will be closing. As Dr. Prathmesh Deshmukh has taken on a new role and will be partially moving to a different city, we can no longer assure the same-day or next-day availability that general practice requires. After much thought, we have taken this difficult decision.

Importantly, we are not closing entirely. Acumed will continue as an exclusive Referral Neurology Clinic, seeing neurology cases by referral on a few days each month.

We will not stop all at once. To help you transition, we are staggering the wind-down: services will reduce through July, continue on limited days until mid-August 2026, and our ongoing acupuncture patients can visit on select days until September 2026.

For routine care, we recommend a trusted vet close to your home. We're happy to help — write to us with your location for suggestions.

Thank you for placing your trust in us. This has been a difficult decision for us too.

Since 2014, it has been our privilege and joy to care for your beloved companions. We are deeply grateful to every pet parent who has walked through our doors and trusted us with the health and wellbeing of their furry family members. Thank you for being a part of our journey.

We have been gradually refining the scope of our practice and reducing the range of general services at our clinic. This has been a thoughtful and ongoing process, and we are now ready to take the next step.

Acumed Veterinary Specialty is transitioning into an exclusive referral neurology practice. Our Out-Patient Department (OPD) and General Practice consultations will be gradually wound down and will cease in the coming months.

Going forward, we will be accepting cases exclusively through veterinary referrals for neurological consultations, diagnostics, and advanced neurology care.
If you have been visiting us for general or routine consultations, we kindly encourage you to connect with a trusted general practice veterinarian in your neighborhood for your pet's ongoing primary care needs. We are happy to help with recommendations if needed.

During this transition over the next few months, our working days may be fewer than usual, and there may be occasional clinic closures that we may not always be able to announce in advance. We truly appreciate your understanding and patience, and we sincerely apologize for any inconvenience.

Updated : May 2026.

featured_reviews.name: sms sweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Smitaa Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a blessing. My German shepherd champ was taken to super pets in an emergency situation. He had developed something called GDV. I was unaware if this situation being a pet parent since more than 17 years now (I have had pets since several years) After taking him to vetic hospital for emergency (which was extremely careless and didn’t even treat it like emergency) post his X-ray on recommendation from some friends I rushed him to super pets. They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. We had to take him for regular follow ups and on a follow up in a weeks time, doctors suspected something wrong and again on further tests discovered that his spleen had got affected and damaged along with few further conditions that had developed. He underwent second surgery. He battled for his life for a month in this hospital. He was hospitalised. The care, affection and love he recieved along with the proper medical care is nothing less than a gift for parents seeing their child fight for life and death each day. Inspite of he being aggressive he was pampered and taken care of as if he belongs to them. His entire body had collapsed and post 1 month he finally got discharged. He had lost his ability to walk post all this condition as his hip and spine had got affected. We continued Physio with them. It’s October today. My boy got discharged in June and we are in our way for our regular Physio all hail and hearty, not just walking but running and bullying my other 2 dogs :) No words can thank them enough. His recovery is nothing less than a miracle only because of timely care and attention given to him by the super vets at super pets.

featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolute lifesavers – Wild Vets Bandra gave my cat Mao Singh a second chance at life!

I can’t thank the team at Wild Vets in Bandra enough**

A few weeks ago, my beloved feline Mao Singh (my ginger-white drama queen) suddenly became critically ill – lethargic, not eating, and hiding all day. I rushed her to Wild Vets and from the moment we walked in, I knew she was in the best hands.
Dr. Nidhi immediately took charge — calm, thorough, and incredibly compassionate. They didn’t waste a second: full in-house blood work, urine analysis, stroke checks (I think they meant biochemistry/profile), and ultrasound (USG) were all done under one roof on the spot. No running around to different labs, no waiting days for results – everything was diagnosed and treated the same day. That comprehensive in-house facility literally saved precious time and, I genuinely believe, saved Mao Singh’s life. Within hours they had her on IV fluids, targeted medication, and close monitoring.
The entire staff was outstanding — special shoutout to Bhaskar and the rest of the assistants who handled my stressed-out cat with so much gentleness and care, keeping me updated every step of the way, even after hours. The clinic is spotless, well-equipped (dedicated cat consult room, ultrasound room, pharmacy stocked with premium medicines), and clearly designed with pets’ comfort in mind — separate dog den and cat corner to reduce stress.

Yes, Wild Vets is not the cheapest vet in town, but when it’s your family member on the line, quality comes at a price — and it’s worth every single rupee. I’d rather pay for expertise, speed, and state-of-the-art facilities than take risks elsewhere.
Today Mao Singh is back home, eating like a champ, zooming around, and giving me her signature judgmental stares

❤️ Thank you from the bottom of my heart to Dr. Nidhi, Dr. Deb, Bhaskar, and the entire Wild Vets family. You didn’t just treat my cat — you gave her (and me) hope and a future. Forever grateful. If you love your pet, this is the only place in Bandra (and probably Mumbai) I’d trust blindly.
Highly recommended — 5 stars aren’t enough! 🐱💙

featured_reviews.name: Sabah Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Update on 16/03/26: Wildvets has now demanded Rs. 1 Lakh in defamation & Rs. 25k for their legal fees in sending me a civil court summon for an honest & truthful review of their practice.

Requesting all pet parents to be extremely cautious while approaching such an establishment.

I have an ongoing treatment for 2 of my cats- there is no doubt that there is  quite of a lot of immoral practice.

21/06/25 - Took my cat “Honey” with a complain of blood in his urine. Drs prescribed a stool, urine, radiograph, & blood test; we agreed & did the radiograph & blood test right there.

Radiograph received on 21st itself, with missing diagnosis that their drs insist we can’t read

Blood reports were a nightmare to get - first admin staff keeps insisting that they’ve sent it over email. I’m receiving other emails from them, they also have the correct email so I guessed it’s some tech issue & requested if she can whatsapp instead. The sheer arrogance of this woman. Downright refusing to do so; Wildvets never gives a hard copy of their reports, & this person is refusing to share it over whatsapp, how am I supposed to see the results? After much arguing she finally agreed to share over whatsapp - what she shares is a stool report from 2024; keep in mind I sent a blood sample in 2025. Explaining her this was another mountain to climb.

23rd - I took my cats Honey and Cream for a sono as Cream also started to show some issues. They did their sono at the clinic itself, in the morning. As of now - 24th June evening - I’m yet to see these reports, keep in mind most places (human or animal) produce these in less than an hour. On 23rd I was told these reports will come by the evening, now I’m being told it will take 3 DAYS?

To top this, their drs injected both my cats with meds their team REFUSED to write down. After we asked the receptionist why so, she exclaimed that all this is in their system. Basically to trap you from going to other vets. Till date I have not recvd a written prescription of what was administered to them. Imagine going to a hospital & them injecting you with whatever, then refusing to disclose? Where is the transparency? Does this not smell of malpractice?

Their drs, despite so many days have been unable to give a clear explanation. Upon seeing the cat’s sono at the clinic they claimed “one was worse than the other”, I’m sorry these educated professionals are calling “worse than the other” a diagnosis? Till date not one of them has explained what results came out of the urinary or stool test. Their drs are always in a rush for “lunch” or “meeting”, I understand prior commitments, but it takes 5 mins to get on a call & explain.

I have been requesting their admin staff to Connect me with dr Amrita but everytime I call it’s a new excuse. This is a common complaint about rude admin staff in their reviews but it seems like the proprietors of the establishment encourage that behavior.

I have so far spent upwards of 25k at their clinic and yet have 0 clear diagnosis, no physical reports (how am I supposed to show radiograph & sono to other drs? On a mobile screen? Or print on a paper? What does wild vets charge a premium for if a report cannot be printed & given? How poor is this place?god only knows how long will the sono take.

I am speaking with 2 other external vets, both of them appalled at Wild Vet’s behavior. Keep in mind I’m not even paying these drs & they have managed to chart a treatment plan, something wild vets is still unable to do. All we do here is x no. of tests to crank up the bill, with drs giving 0 explanations, admin staff disrespecting you at every chance they get, & a potential malpractice of injecting animals with substances that can make their situation worse. They won’t let you take a simple file to store prescription without paying for it, but they will ensure to milk you dry out of money until your wallet dies or your pet.

I’m sure Wildvets will have a long defensive answer to give, I’m keen on knowing what justifies rudeness, lack of communication, & refusal to write down administered meds

featured_reviews.name: Preeti Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my dog, Coco, to Wild Vets for a rabies titre test as part of the requirements for traveling to Dubai. Unfortunately, I had a disappointing experience with their service and communication.
Firstly, I was not informed that the sample could be sent to a lab in Bangalore, which is recognized by the UAE government. Instead, they chose to send it to a lab in London that charges £70 (as per the lab's website). However, I was charged ₹24,800 by Wild Vets, which is a significant markup with no clear explanation provided.
The sample was taken on August 9th, and I was told that I would receive the results within 3 to 4 weeks. As the three-week mark passed, I began following up and learned from the London lab that the results had already been sent to Wild Vets. Despite this, I did not receive the results promptly.
When I contacted Dr. Amrita for clarity, I was shocked by how rudely I was spoken to, especially considering the amount I had paid for the service. Due to these delays and lack of proper communication, I was forced to postpone my travel plans. I finally received the test results after five weeks — far beyond the promised timeline.
This entire experience has left me disappointed and frustrated. I no longer feel confident in the professionalism or reliability of the doctors at Wild Vets.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am reporting this to relevant authorities as Vetic wants to shield the negligence.

Formal Complaint: Negligence in Post-Operative Care Resulting in Death of Cat – Indra (01.01.2025)
I am writing this email with deep grief and distress to formally report negligence and lack of due medical care by your veterinarian at Vetic Kandivali, which resulted in the death of my cat, Indra.

On 01.01.2025, I brought Indra, a free-roaming cat under my care, to your Kandivali clinic as he was bleeding from the mouth. After examination, your veterinarian diagnosed that Indra’s teeth were broken and decayed and advised that dental extraction was required. The procedure was carried out at your clinic.

Post-procedure, Indra was safely kept in a cage at his usual location for observation. However, he bled excessively through the night. Early the next morning, I immediately brought Indra back to the same veterinarian and showed him clear photographs evidencing significant blood loss from the mouth.

Despite being presented with visible proof of continuous bleeding after a dental procedure, the veterinarian stated that he “could not see any bleeding points” in the mouth and took no corrective or preventive action. No emergency intervention, no saline support, no observation, and no admission for monitoring was advised or initiated. Indra was sent back with me.

Within approximately one hour of returning, Indra began bleeding again. I immediately called the same veterinarian and informed him that the bleeding had resumed. At this point, instead of addressing the emergency himself, he advised me to consult another veterinarian from the same clinic chain, stating that a senior doctor there “might be more competent.”

This statement itself is alarming. If the treating veterinarian believed he was not competent to handle a post-operative complication, he should have escalated the matter immediately in the morning itself, retained the cat under observation, or ensured emergency stabilisation. Sending a bleeding animal away without monitoring or intervention amounts to gross negligence.

Due to the failure to act in time and the lack of appropriate post-operative care, Indra continued to bleed and ultimately passed away.

I request the following from your end within 7 days of receipt of this email:

A complete written explanation of the diagnosis, dental procedure performed, and post-operative assessment.

Clarification on why no emergency measures or observation were initiated despite clear signs of blood loss.

Details of the veterinarian(s) involved, including qualifications and roles.

Please note that this email is being sent as a formal record. In the absence of a satisfactory response, I will be constrained to escalate this matter to the State Veterinary Council, Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, and other appropriate authorities for negligence and deficiency in service.

This communication is written in pain, but also with the expectation of accountability from a professional medical establishment.

Sincerely,

featured_reviews.name: Aaliya Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Vetic Pet Vet in Kandivali with my cat Lucky, and I can confidently say it was one of the best veterinary experiences I’ve ever had. From the moment we entered, everything felt extremely well-organized, clean, and welcoming.
The staff members were very polite, calm, and friendly. They treated both pets and pet parents with a lot of respect and patience, which instantly made me feel comfortable. The doctor explained everything in a very clear and simple way, making sure all my doubts were answered properly. I really appreciated how carefully and gently Lucky was handled.
The clinic itself is beautifully maintained. The lighting is excellent, the space is hygienic, and even basic facilities like clean drinking water are thoughtfully provided. These small details show how much care and planning has gone into creating a comfortable environment.
One of the cutest and most heart-warming moments was seeing a cat at the entrance, almost like a little welcome host 🥰 It immediately made the place feel pet-friendly and positive.
Overall, the professionalism, cleanliness, and genuine care shown by the staff and doctors truly stood out. Vetic Pet Vet is a place where pets are treated with love and responsibility, and pet parents can feel relaxed and confident.

I would highly recommend Vetic Pet Vet, Kandivali to anyone looking for high-quality veterinary care and a truly pleasant experience for their pets.

featured_reviews.name: Preshit Deorukhkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE. AVOID!

I had an extremely disappointing experience here. When I enquired about lab tests for my dog, I was clearly told the tests would cost ₹1,250 and the consultation ₹600. However, after the visit, we were billed ₹3,000 for the reports and ₹799 for the consultation — more than double the quoted amount. This discrepancy only came to light after we had already paid. It felt completely misleading and dishonest.

On top of that, they actively try to upsell their membership by sweet-talking customers into it, without being transparent about the actual value or necessity.

The medicines prescribed by the doctor were not available in the required quantities. We were promised home delivery the next day, but it took three full days and multiple follow-ups to receive them — and even then, the order was incomplete, with missing medicines and no mention or update that items were pending.

The only saving grace in this entire experience was Dr. Sudarshan and the support staff, who were genuinely kind, caring, and courteous. Thank you, Doctor — you and your team’s professionalism deserve better management and more honest practices.

This review is being written to formally document my extremely distressing experience with Nagares Animal Care Clinic regarding the treatment of my dog.

I entrusted this clinic with the care and medical treatment of my dog with the expectation of professional conduct, transparency, and proper veterinary care. Unfortunately, my dog did not survive. Throughout the treatment process, there was a serious lack of clear communication regarding my dog’s medical condition, the procedures being carried out, and the associated risks.

As a pet owner going through a critical medical situation, I expected honest explanations, compassionate handling, and ethical veterinary practice. Instead, the experience left me feeling that financial demands were prioritized while important medical information was not adequately explained.

Another highly concerning issue was that a staff member who attempted to cooperate and provide support during this situation was reportedly dismissed shortly afterwards. This raises serious concerns about the internal practices and professional environment of the clinic.

The loss of a pet is emotionally devastating. For many of us, our pets are not just animals — they are like our children and family members. The way this situation was handled has only deepened that pain.

As a pet parent, I urge other pet parents to be extremely cautious.
